candidates.name: epfl-dlab/GoogleTrendsAnchorBank (gtab)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (123 stars, MIT, 217 commits) that builds an offline 'anchor bank' of pre-calibrated Google Trends queries spanning the full popularity spectrum, then calibrates any new query against it via binary search so results are comparable across time and across >5-query batches, avoiding Trends' integer-rounding and 5-term comparison limit. Published method (West, CIKM 2020).
candidates.why_useful: Direct hit on CONTEXT gap #4/#17: the team's own Google Trends test failed because raw pulls are not point-in-time and not comparable across pulls; gtab is exactly the 'anchored Google Trends' tooling flagged as a method still worth trying before writing off Trends entirely as a nights/engagement nowcast input.
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as Google Trends allows (2004-present), calibrated
candidates.size_hint: library + anchor-bank config files, not a bulk dataset
candidates.last_activity: 217 commits on master (exact date not surfaced)

candidates.name: mortada/fredapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python wrapper (1.7k stars, Apache-2.0, 67 commits) around both FRED and ALFRED (Archival FRED), returning pandas objects; explicitly supports pulling data 'as it was known' on a given vintage date, i.e. true point-in-time macro revision histories, not just current-vintage series.
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT gap #4 explicitly wants 'ALFRED-style macro vintages'; this is the standard client for exactly that (CPI, PCE, etc. as-reported-then vs as-revised-now), useful for building a genuinely point-in-time consumer-strength or macro control panel to test against nights, rather than the current-vintage-only FRED series the team already holds.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by series, many back to 1940s-60s, vintages from ALFRED's start (~1990s for most series)
candidates.last_activity: 67 commits on master (exact date not surfaced)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends the FRED holding (~40 series) to vintage/point-in-time mode, which the current holding is not

candidates.name: openskynetwork/opensky-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python/Java client (466 stars, GPL-3.0, 175 commits) for the OpenSky Network REST API: real-time and (via the separate Impala historical database access, same org) historical ADS-B aircraft state vectors — positions, altitude, velocity, callsign — for commercial and general aviation globally. OAuth2 now mandatory (since Mar 2026).
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT gap #10 (airline/rail capacity) names OpenSky/ADS-B directly; flight volumes by route/region are a leading indicator of cross-border travel demand and could proxy inbound tourism intensity for APAC/LatAm/EMEA mix ahead of official aviation stats.
candidates.time_coverage: live states since ~2013; historical bulk access requires separate Impala/Trino shell, rate-limited for free tier
candidates.size_hint: API only; historical bulk pulls are large (TB-scale) and gated
candidates.last_activity: 175 commits on master (exact date not surfaced), actively maintained (2026 OAuth2 update)

candidates.name: jpatokal/openflights
candidates.what_it_holds: The OpenFlights.org codebase and its committed /data directory: static tables of ~7,000+ airports, ~6,000 airlines, and ~67,000 routes (origin-destination-airline), AGPL-3.0, 1,487 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Not a KPI time series but a clean route-network reference table; useful as a join key / weighting scheme to turn airline capacity or airport-passenger stats (gap #10) into a regional travel-intensity index by market, cheaper than building an airport list from scratch.
candidates.time_coverage: static snapshot, periodically updated, not a time series
candidates.size_hint: a few MB of CSV/DAT files

candidates.name: facundoolano/app-store-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js module (1.4k stars, MIT, 164 commits) that pulls current iTunes/App Store app metadata, search results, developer pages, reviews/ratings, version history and 'similar apps' — a snapshot scraper, not a ranking-history store.
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT gap #5 wants app download/ranking history as an engagement proxy for Airbnb's own app; this tool can pull Airbnb's current App Store rank/rating/review volume on a schedule to build a point-in-time series going forward (does not recover history retroactively), and the review text stream is a free sentiment/complaint source (e.g. cancellation/RNPL friction mentions).
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only; a history has to be built by running it repeatedly
candidates.last_activity: 164 commits on master (exact date not surfaced)

candidates.name: OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Official repo (341 stars, 1,892 commits, updated as recently as 12 Sep 2026) behind tracktherecovery.org: aggregated, de-identified card-spend, employment, and job-postings series broken out by US county, industry, and income quartile, plus a data dictionary and a documented revisions history.
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT already lists 'Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker card spend' as held, but this is the actual repo, actively updated in Sep 2026, with county- and income-quartile-level granularity (finer than a single national series) — useful for a leisure-vs-necessity or high-income-traveler spend cut that could lead ABNB's higher-income guest base ahead of national retail-sales prints.
candidates.time_coverage: 2020-present, updated through Sep 2026 per commit history
candidates.size_hint: multiple CSV tables, tens of MB
candidates.license: free use with attribution; no commercial resale of underlying data
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker card spend panel (already held) — flag because this source is county/income-quartile granular and actively updated, finer than what CONTEXT describes

candidates.name: rohitgodbole/WikiPageviews
candidates.what_it_holds: A thin wrapper (0 stars) around the official Wikimedia Pageviews API, updated as recently as 26 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT gap #5 flags 'Wikipedia pageviews tooling' explicitly; pageviews for 'Airbnb', 'Vrbo', destination-city pages, or 'short-term rental' articles are free, dated-by-day, genuinely point-in-time (the API returns historical daily counts as originally recorded) and could proxy search/engagement interest as an alternative to non-point-in-time Google Trends. The official Wikimedia REST pageviews API itself (no wrapper needed) is the more load-bearing artifact here; this repo is just one thin client example.
candidates.time_coverage: Wikimedia pageviews API covers July 2015-present daily/hourly, official and point-in-time

candidates.name: microlinkhq/cloudflare-bot-directory
candidates.what_it_holds: A committed JSON dataset (18 stars, updated 14 Sep 2026) of 500+ verified bots and web crawlers sourced from Cloudflare Radar — names, user-agent patterns, categories, robots.txt compliance, operator.
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT gap #19 (AI-referral traffic / bot-crawler share) names Cloudflare Radar directly; this is a maintained, machine-readable snapshot of the bot taxonomy Radar tracks, useful as a reference table for classifying AI-agent vs human traffic in any web-log or Common Crawl work the team already has (the Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com), though it is not itself a time series of bot traffic share.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot, actively maintained (last commit same day as this scout)
candidates.license: code MIT; data CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial only)

candidates.name: bgpkit/radar-rs
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial Rust SDK (2 stars, MIT) for the Cloudflare Radar API — global internet traffic, outage, and protocol-adoption data.
candidates.why_useful: Another thin client for Radar's traffic-rank and outage endpoints (gap #5/#19: web-traffic-estimate style engagement proxies and bot/AI traffic); low value on its own since it is an unofficial low-star wrapper, but confirms Radar's API is the right target and is scriptable outside Rust via its plain REST endpoints too.

candidates.name: kuandeng/LightGCN
candidates.what_it_holds: Recommendation-systems repo that bundles a processed version of the Gowalla location check-in dataset (train.txt/test.txt user-item interaction lists plus user_list.txt/item_list.txt ID maps) alongside Yelp2018 and Amazon-book, as inputs to a graph recommender.
candidates.why_useful: CONTEXT gap #20 names Gowalla/Foursquare check-ins as party-size / cross-border tourism-flow proxies; this repo's Gowalla data is however already reduced to anonymous user-POI interaction pairs for a recommender (no raw lat/lon/timestamp), so it would need re-derivation from the original SNAP Gowalla release to recover geospatial/temporal check-in patterns — flagging as a lead, not a ready-made dataset.
candidates.geography: originally global (Gowalla was worldwide, US/EU heavy)
candidates.time_coverage: Gowalla operated 2007-2012 (service later shut down); dataset reflects that window only
candidates.size_hint: processed text files, tens of MB
candidates.license: not stated for data; code unspecified

candidates.name: thekingofkings/gowalla-exp
candidates.what_it_holds: 13-star repo doing trajectory-based analysis/experiments on the Gowalla check-in dataset.
candidates.why_useful: A second lead toward the raw(er) Gowalla check-in geodata (with trajectories, implying lat/lon/time preserved) rather than LightGCN's ID-only reduction; worth a closer read if the team wants a pre-2013 geotagged mobility panel as a structural (not current) party-size/cross-border proxy per gap #20.

candidates.name: pengwynn/gowalla
candidates.what_it_holds: Ruby wrapper (56 stars) for the (now-defunct) Gowalla API.
candidates.why_useful: Historical-interest only — Gowalla shut down in 2012 so this API client is dead; listed only to close out the idea for the next scout so it is not re-flagged.
candidates.last_activity: 2025-06-08 (repo housekeeping only, underlying API dead since 2012)

notes: Ten wildcard ideas hunted this pass (a quant-nowcast lens, not 'Airbnb' searches): (1) anchored/calibrated Google Trends tooling as a fix for the team's failed raw-Trends test -- HIT (gtab); (2) ALFRED/FRED point-in-time macro vintage clients -- HIT (fredapi); (3) flight-tracking/airline-route capacity data as a cross-border travel proxy -- HIT (OpenSky, OpenFlights); (4) app-store scraping for Airbnb's own app engagement/rank as a demand proxy -- PARTIAL HIT (app-store-scraper gets snapshots and reviews, not historical rank -- a history would have to be built forward from today, it can't be backfilled); (5) the Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker repo itself, checked for finer granularity than what's already held -- HIT, confirmed county/income-quartile cuts and live Sep-2026 updates, flagged as a granularity upgrade not a new source; (6) Wikipedia pageviews tooling for destination/brand search-interest as a point-in-time-friendly Trends substitute -- weak HIT (thin wrapper found; the underlying official Wikimedia pageviews REST API is the real asset and needs no wrapper); (7) Cloudflare Radar bot/AI-crawler taxonomy and traffic-rank APIs for the 'AI-referral traffic' gap -- weak HIT (a maintained bot directory and two thin unofficial SDKs, no ready time series); (8) geotagged check-in datasets (Gowalla/Foursquare) as party-size/group-travel/cross-border mobility proxies -- WEAK/PARTIAL: Gowalla leads exist but the widely-reused version (LightGCN etc.) is ID-only, stripped of lat/lon/time; a raw-with-coordinates copy needs more digging (thekingofkings/gowalla-exp is the better lead), and Gowalla only covers 2007-2012 so it's a structural-pattern source at best, not current; Foursquare NYC/Tokyo check-in dataset searches were rate-limited before a repo could be confirmed -- FOLLOW UP; (9) cruise-line advance-ticket-sale / booking-curve data (NCLH) as a 'book-ahead business' kernel analogue per gap #18 -- MISS, nothing found on GitHub in the time available (cruise lines don't appear to have any open booking-curve data mirrored); (10) digital-nomad / remote-work survey data (Nomad List, WFH Research SWAA) per gap #16 -- UNRESOLVED, all searches hit either the WebSearch session budget (exhausted platform-wide, not just this scout) or GitHub's unauthenticated web-search 429 (Retry-After 3600s) before a repo could be confirmed or ruled out -- FOLLOW UP with a fresh WebSearch budget or `gh search repos` once the primary rate limit resets (hit 403 repeatedly after ~4-5 calls in quick succession; each reset took about 40s for the primary limit but the secondary/abuse limit on unauthenticated github.com/search pages held for a full hour). Process note for the next scout: WebSearch was already at its session cap before this run started (0 successful WebSearch calls made), so this catalogue leans entirely on `gh search repos` (hit primary + secondary rate limits repeatedly) and direct WebFetch of specific known repo URLs (reliable) rather than WebFetch of github.com/search result pages (429'd every time, unauthenticated). Recommend the next wildcard scout open with `gh auth status` and pace `gh search repos` calls at least 10-15s apart, and prefer direct repo-URL WebFetch over site-search WebFetch throughout.
